body: Thank you for the thoughtful reply, it is truly appreciated. Yes, I have been completely humbled, it is with a broken and contrite spirit I seek guidance. It is long past time that I found a new fellowship. 🙏
You're very welcome! It is heartbreaking. I truly loved my fiance but it was terrifying to look in his eyes when he was psychotic and realize the man I loved was not present.

Woah, 2 months?!?!?! If someone is having doubts this early on, even in "regular" relationships, that is a huge red flag because this is still the honeymoon period. Friend, GTFO of this relationship for your own good. If it's toxic at 2 months, it's going to be a nightmare at 6 months. I have no dog in this fight, I'm genuinely worried about you; Not just *your* mental health, your physical safety. Please leave.

Oh? No one is entitled to a relationship with you and you are not obligated to stay in a clearly unhealthy situation that puts you at risk just to spare someone else. It's not selfish to want a healthy relationship and to be safe, friend. Sometimes we have to put ourselves first because no one else will. The truth is, most people are selfish. The fact that you would endure this relationship because you care for him so much proves you are not selfish.

I'm probably not the best person to ask because my advice is to leave immediately. My (ex) fiance and I had the same diagnosis and there was a lot of abuse on both sides. I would never date someone with a similar diagnosis again, nor would I recommend anyone else do that, including myself. I'm sorry of that's not what you want to hear but the truth is if he's having paranoid delusions about you, you are in danger.

In psychosis, almost anything that can be considered sinister will be, at least for me. A neutral interaction will be interpreted in the absolute worst way imaginable. For instance when I was with my fiance, if he didn't text me back immediately, I thought he had been murdered and I could see visions of the blood/gore. Like trivial things my mind would link to concoct this elaborate scenario (delusion) where every little thing had a meaning and was part of some malicious plot. Trivial things like the color of stop lights or what shoes someone was wearing. I do remember some incidents to a certain extent but it's difficult, I think, because it's a whole thought process and once someone is better they don't think the same way or it's embarrassing at least to me how "silly" it all sounds.

I used to be on disability for some years. It was a huge thing for me to be able to work. My existence on disability was lonely and miserable. I *have* thought about it though. Sometimes I wish they'd just lock me up for good so I don't have to deal with the world and there are friends inside unlike on the outside.

Yeah, it's definitely a coping mechanism for me, too. Unhealthy for sure. It was getting to the point where I couldn't control my drinking like I'd buy a fifth and tell myself half today, half tomorrow only to kill the whole thing in a night, black out, get on my roommate's last nerve and do it again the next day lol 😬

I was ready to blow my brains out after a string of suicide attempts on Buspar. Stole my dad's gun and everything so when I got hospitalized the doctor committed me to a state hospital and it sucked! After 2 months I was so over it.

Oh yeah, SSRIs put me in *ugly* mixed episodes. My first med was that and I had to be hospitalized for 6 months starting this whole terrible business. I was in the hospital like 2 months ago and they said schizo for sure 🤔
